text.p: British security products group Williams Holdings Plc said on Friday it would continue to stomp the acquisition trail after it bought Tesa, a Spanish commercial and residential security products maker.

"Our strategy is to continue to strengthen our position in fire and security home improvement products...We are ambitious for continued growth and expansion and will continue to buy businesses to do just that," chief executive Roger Carr said in a telephone interview.
Including Tesa, Williams has pumped around 330 million stg into 10 acquisitions this year to expand its security products and fire protection divisions.
It sold its British building products businesses for 360 million earlier this month in a move to refocus the group and enhance growth prospects, Carr said.
The deal to buy Tesa, which Williams called the market leader in Spain for commercial and residential security and number two in the world electronic hotel lock market, will cost 101 million stg.
Tesa, based in Irun, northern Spain, expects profit before interest and tax of around $19 million and sales of $153 million in the year to December 31, 1996.
Carr said the acquisition would "totally" complement the product range of its security products division, which manufactures and distributes locks under the Yale brand name.
"This is a very substantial growth in our security interests and very important to Yale internationally...Given our global spread, it will really move the business and Yale on," he said.
Carr said much of Tesa's growth had come from the hotel lock business, with the U.S. accounting for most of the Spanish group's sales.
"Within the sales mix, about 40 percent is the access control electronics side, and it has been the hotel market which has been the primary driver," Carr said.
The Tesa deal includes a newly-established factory in low-cost Mexico which Carr described as a crucial pillar of Tesa's export-oriented business.
